the PD material is better than anything a permissive-but-modern search

They are also honest about what they are: a nineteenth-century painting of
the Ides of March is a Roman scene imagined by a Roman-obsessed age, not
evidence. The credit line under each plate says the artist and the year, so
a reader can see they are looking at 1805 rather than 44 BC.
